recent_lane_artifacts.note: At run inspection time, data/automation contained only README.md and collection-policy.v1.json; no completed lane subdirectories/artifacts were yet present on automation-research. This run therefore used current Foundation/consumer contracts plus fresh external evidence.

results.summary: Five recurring concepts were examined. Four are mature enough to standardize as Universal metric/record candidates without creating a new top-level domain. One should remain observation-first until semantics are validated across more independent ecosystems. Existing flexible research-bundle metric storage can already retain all of them; promotion means controlled semantics and collection-profile guidance, not a hard storage boundary.

field_candidates.definition: Elapsed time required for the gross contribution generated by an acquired customer/account/cohort to recover the fully loaded acquisition cost attributable to that acquisition.

temporal_semantics.note: Do not mix acquisition cohort date, reporting period, and observation date.

methodology.preferred: reported value when the source defines its method
methodology.warning: Do not derive when CAC is blended across an incompatible segment or when ARPA/gross margin periods do not align.

field_candidates.denominator: one newly acquired customer/account, or an explicitly defined acquisition cohort

source_provenance.origin_policy: reported if directly disclosed; derived only when all components are evidenced and formula/basis are retained

field_candidates.why_material: Absolute CAC alone does not reveal whether the business can recycle acquisition capital before customers churn. Payback converts acquisition spend into a cash-time constraint and is directly comparable across many recurring or repeat-purchase models when basis is explicit.
field_candidates.version_policy: v1 requires months plus basis metadata. Any future alternative contribution-margin or cash-basis definition must use a new methodology_version rather than silently changing the formula.
field_candidates.backfill_selection_rule: Select entities with reported CAC payback OR with compatible CAC + ARPA/average gross contribution + gross margin data; prioritize paid-acquisition, B2B sales, subscription, agency retainer, and repeat-purchase cases.

field_candidates.definition: A measured transition from a named upstream stage/event to a named downstream stage/event, retaining both counts and the rule that defines a successful transition rather than storing only a naked conversion percentage.
field_candidates.unit: count + percent; optional duration in seconds/hours/days

methodology.warning: Conversion rates are not comparable if entry event, counting unit, ordering rule, or conversion window differs.

field_candidates.denominator: number of eligible entrants into stage_from under the declared counting rule

source_provenance.origin_policy: reported/observed preferred; estimates must preserve how stage counts were inferred

field_candidates.why_material: The current profiles capture channels, first customers, demand and retention but not where demand is lost between attention, signup/lead, activation and payment. A stage-pair representation works across SaaS, commerce, lead generation, marketplaces and onboarding without forcing one product-specific funnel.
field_candidates.version_policy: v1 uses a generic stage-pair object. Do not hard-code canonical funnel stages globally; product/domain-specific stage taxonomies may be versioned separately.
field_candidates.backfill_selection_rule: Select cases with public visitor/lead/signup/trial/activation/checkout/purchase counts, disclosed conversion rates, onboarding metrics, sales pipeline counts, or screenshots/reports containing two or more funnel stages.

field_candidates.definition: Period-specific change in recurring revenue classified by economic cause: new business, expansion, contraction, churn, reactivation, or neutral change.
field_candidates.unit: currency per normalized recurring period, normally MRR or ARR

temporal_semantics.note: Retain original billing interval separately from normalized MRR/ARR.

methodology.warning: Do not collapse logo churn and revenue churn; expansion can mask a leaking customer base.

field_candidates.denominator: for movement amounts, none; for derived retention ratios, opening recurring revenue of the defined customer cohort

source_provenance.origin_policy: reported movement preferred; derived classification allowed only from evidenced subscription changes

field_candidates.why_material: A single retention/churn field loses the mechanism of recurring-revenue change. Separating expansion, contraction, churn and reactivation explains whether growth comes from new logos, deeper monetization, winback, or merely offsets leakage.
field_candidates.version_policy: v1 defines the six movement classes. Future billing-edge cases may add subtypes but must preserve these top-level classes for longitudinal comparability.
field_candidates.backfill_selection_rule: Select recurring-revenue entities with public MRR histories, plan upgrade/downgrade/cancel/reactivation data, cohort retention reports, or source systems that expose subscription movement history.

field_candidates.definition: Revenue contractually committed under existing customer arrangements but not yet recognized, retaining whether it is billed/deferred, unbilled/backlog, current, or noncurrent when the source distinguishes those components.

methodology.warning: Do not treat all sales pipeline or non-binding bookings as contracted future revenue.

field_candidates.denominator: not applicable; stock amount at a point in time

source_provenance.origin_policy: reported only unless a contract schedule explicitly supports calculation

field_candidates.why_material: Current revenue/MRR/ARR describe what has been recognized or normalized now; contracted future revenue describes visibility and commitment already locked in. It recurs across enterprise software, consulting, industrial/service contracts and other backlog-driven models and materially changes risk assessment.
field_candidates.version_policy: v1 stores a broad canonical concept plus source-native subtype. Accounting-defined RPO must remain distinguishable from operational order backlog.
field_candidates.backfill_selection_rule: Select public companies and private cases with RPO/cRPO/deferred revenue/backlog/order-book disclosures; prioritize contract-heavy SaaS, enterprise software, services, manufacturing, construction and long-term support businesses.

field_candidates.definition: Observed cumulative revenue or gross contribution generated by a defined acquisition cohort as cohort age increases, stored as realized points rather than a single modeled lifetime-value estimate.
field_candidates.unit: currency per original customer/account; optional retention percent

methodology.warning: Do not store modeled LTV as if it were realized value. Keep forecasts and realized cohort curves separate.

field_candidates.denominator: original customers/accounts in the declared acquisition cohort

source_provenance.origin_policy: observation-first because current evidence is strong but concentrated in subscription analytics; seek independent commerce/marketplace/service evidence before typed promotion

field_candidates.why_material: ChartMogul's 2026 research reports that 28.3% of cohorts differ from actual revenue by more than 50% under common LTV approaches. A realized curve preserves what actually happened and prevents a single estimated LTV from hiding cohort heterogeneity.
field_candidates.version_policy: Remain untyped observation until at least one additional independent ecosystem confirms a stable cross-model representation. If promoted, forecast LTV and realized value must be separate metric families.
field_candidates.backfill_selection_rule: For now, collect as Observation when a source exposes cohort retention/revenue by age. Do not launch broad backfill until semantics are validated outside SaaS/subscription analytics.

non_promotions.concept: website/app traffic and workforce growth signals
non_promotions.reason: Dealroom and Similarweb show that traffic, MAU, engagement, traffic-source mix and workforce growth are useful leading signals, but Foundation's generic Metric records can already represent them and current collection scope already calls for public traffic/SEO/hiring signals. The immediate need is a controlled metric_type vocabulary and source-methodology metadata, not another top-level field.

Material, but already covered by current pricing scope (annual/buyout/prepay) and cash-timing/negative-working-capital collection guidance. Standardize values inside existing structures rather than create a duplicate field.

Material and repeatedly used in acquisition diligence, but current 12-domain scope already explicitly includes concentration risk. Improve typed metric coverage (largest_customer_revenue_share, top_n_revenue_share) within that domain instead of treating it as a novel concept.

observations.text: research-bundle.v1 already permits arbitrary metric_type strings with value, unit, time, basis, scope, origin, confidence and evidence. Therefore EVOLVE should prefer semantic registries/profile guidance over adding rigid top-level storage fields whenever a concept can be represented as a Metric.

Current business-intelligence products increasingly expose time-series leading signals (traffic, MAU, workforce growth, hiring) alongside lagging financials. Similarweb documents traffic/engagement/source datasets with up to 61 months of history, while Dealroom company profiles expose monthly traffic and workforce growth signals.

Single summary metrics are often semantically lossy. Funnel conversion needs stage/window/counting definitions; retention needs expansion/contraction/churn distinctions; LTV estimates can deviate materially from realized cohort revenue. New semantics should preserve components and methodology rather than add opaque scalar fields.

errors.detail: No backfill/discovery/monitor run artifacts existed on automation-research at inspection time, so this EVOLVE run could not mine cross-lane observations yet. Re-check those lanes on the next EVOLVE execution.
